findings.text: non-blocking: content_digest's read stores decoded text with memoized("plan_text", target, lambda: text), and memoized keys that store on the stat signature taken after the lambda returns, so a write landing between file_bytes' read and this store caches the old text under the new signature; the content_digest entry itself is shielded by memoized's post-compute recheck, but the plan_text entry is already stored and _read_plan_text/plan_text readers serve it. The pre-existing metadata_index._content_digest guards this by re-reading when file_signature(path) != signature (reckon/metadata_index.py:923-929); the new copy drops the guard.

non-blocking: the diff adds file_memo.content_digest, which duplicates _content_digest still present here — same sha256 of the bytes, the same memoised kind "content_digest" and the same plan_text priming — rather than moving the owner's body into file_memo and having this module call it; two implementations of one capability now coexist, one with the stale-text guard and one without.
